plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid (which is what you'd pay), and truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Since this is a single round with no repeated learning needed, and the format matches standard Vickrey auction rules, I will bid exactly my value of $33 to ensure optimal expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid), which means the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (profitable) and lose when it doesn't (avoiding losses), while paying only the second-highest bid regardless of what I bid. Since this is a single round with no repeated interaction effects to exploit, truthful bidding is optimal. My value is $10, so I will bid $10.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're highest). Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if you win against a bid between your value and your bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single round with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my true value of $21 to maximize expected profit.
